doc.title: Benny Golson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: New York, Bostic and Dizzy Gillespie
title: Quincy Jones's publishing and rooming together on Dizzy's tours
summary: Golson got publishing back from Quincy Jones without trouble; they were friends and roommates, two to a room on the road with Gillespie.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Did Quincy Jones at any time own any of your publishing?

Oh yeah. But I decided – Quincy had Silhouette – I decided, why don’t I get things back under my own umbrella? With him it was no problem. I got those things back. No problem with him. We were friends. We used to live in the same building together. I was fourth floor. He was sixth floor. And we were boys. We used to be roommates. So there was no problem.

Um-hmm. Not in New York. Traveling with Dizzy’s band. It was always two to a room. Now it’s one to a room. But it was two to a room then. That two to a room, we got to – I can’t talk about that. Quincy Jones. My man.
I know that when I interviewed Al McKibbon, he talked about rooming with Chano [Pozo], touring with Diz’s band. So there’s a long history and legacy with two . . .
. . . with the two beds. One wants to do something – yeah. Those were good days though.
